findings.label: Paid During Active Breaches
findings.detail: 4 suppliers received payments while in breach of Companies Act — including 0 critical and 0 high severity. Temporally verified against payment dates.

findings.label: Likely Duplicate Payments
findings.detail: 105 high-confidence duplicate groups with same supplier, amount, date and reference (3+ copies) (after filtering 571 CSV republication artifacts)
findings.context_note: Quarterly CSV overlaps (same transaction appearing in 2 files) have been filtered out. Remaining duplicates show 3+ identical copies, which are more likely genuine overpayments.

findings.label: Round-Number Payments (>£5K)
findings.detail: 836 exact round-number payments over £5,000 — may indicate estimates rather than invoiced amounts

findings.label: Year-End Spending Pattern
findings.detail: Staffs C.C. Precept spent 4.9x their monthly average in March (£11.5M above normal). Note: UK councils operate on April–March fiscal years, so elevated March spending is common as departments finalise annual budgets. Spikes above 3x warrant further scrutiny.
findings.context_note: March spending above the monthly average is expected for UK councils on April–March fiscal years. Compare against prior years' March figures for meaningful analysis.

findings.label: Rapid Payment Suppliers
findings.detail: 13 suppliers receive payments every <14 days on average. Top: Equans Regeneration Ltd (8.6 day avg, 1374 payments, £31.5M)

findings.label: Benford's Law Anomaly
findings.detail: Significant deviation from Benford's Law (p < 0.001). Digit 3 deviates 5.3% from expected distribution across 23,516 transactions. Note: with 23,516 transactions, chi-squared tests are highly sensitive — the 5.3% max digit deviation is the more practical measure of anomaly.
findings.context_note: Chi-squared values on samples of 23,516+ transactions are naturally inflated and will almost always show statistical significance. The max digit deviation (5.3%) is a more meaningful indicator — deviations under 5% are typical for legitimate council spending.

findings.label: Second-Digit Benford's Anomaly
findings.detail: Second-digit distribution across 23,560 transactions shows p < 0.001 (highly significant). Digit 0 deviates 7.15% from Nigrini's expected distribution. Second-digit tests are more discriminating than first-digit for detecting round-number bias and fabricated invoices.
findings.context_note: Benford's second-digit analysis (Nigrini, 2012) uses chi-squared with 9 df. Critical values: 16.92 (p=0.05), 21.67 (p=0.01), 27.88 (p=0.001). n=23,560.

key_findings.title: 2 suppliers with clock-like payment regularity
key_findings.description: These suppliers receive payments at near-identical intervals (std dev <5 days). Top: Susan Latimer — every 30.2 days (23 payments, £11.5K)

key_findings.description: Averaging £22.9K per transaction — the council's most frequent supplier
